back: An agreement in which a franchisor allows a franchisee to trade under its brand and methods in return for fees and royalties.
Franchisor: owner of the brand who grants the right. Franchisee: the person who pays to trade under the brand.
An agreement between two or more businesses to set up and share the ownership, risk and reward of a project or new business.
A business that trades to meet a social or environmental purpose and reinvests most of its profit in it.

front: Benefits and drawbacks of a franchise
back: Franchisee: proven brand and support but fees, royalties and less freedom. Franchisor: faster growth but risk to its brand.
Shared cost, risk and skills; but possible disagreement, culture clashes and shared profit.
Compare liability, finance, control, risk, tax and administration, and the owner's purpose.
Owned by the state or local authority; aim to provide a service rather than maximise profit.
Royalty = percentage rate × revenue, paid regularly by a franchisee to the franchisor.
